entry.title: Syscall Series #3 - Hell's Hall
entry.summary: Hell’s Hall is an indirect syscall technique that executes syscall instructions from system DLLs other than ntdll.dll, typically kernel32.dll. By making the return address appear to originate from a trusted DLL, it evades kernel instrumentation callbacks that would flag syscalls executing from ntdll.dll directly. entry.title: Syscall Series #2 - Tartarus' Gate
entry.summary: Tartarus’ Gate is a dynamic syscall discovery technique that locates syscall numbers in adjacent functions when the target function is hooked. Rather than searching within the function itself, it searches neighboring functions, exploiting the sequential organization of syscalls in ntdll. entry.title: Syscall Series #1 - Hell's Gate
entry.summary: EDR vendors have spent years hooking NTDLL functions to intercept suspicious API calls. Hell’s Gate, published in 2019, offered a clean answer: skip NTDLL entirely and invoke syscalls directly, extracting the SSN from memory at runtime so nothing is hardcoded and no hook is ever hit.
